While the 90% confidence intervals capture the most probable range of outcomes, certain high-impact, low-probability events could push the actual value outside these bounds. On the downside, a sudden, severe economic recession, an unexpected major geopolitical conflict escalation, a significant regulatory crackdown, or a "black swan" event like a new global health crisis could trigger a sharp market sell-off, driving the value significantly below the lower end of the monthly interval.
